citation: Douillard JY, Oliner KS, Siena S, et al. Panitumumab-FOLFOX4 treatment and RAS mutations in colorectal cancer. N Engl J Med. 2013;369(11):1023-34.
data_source: PubMed abstract (PMID 24024839) + AACR abstract (Hecht 2014, doi:10.1158/1557-3125.RASONC14-A57) + Douillard 2015 Eur J Cancer (PMID 25892681, tumor shrinkage/RAS WT n=505)

ras_subgroups.mutation_detail: WT for KRAS exons 2/3/4 AND NRAS exons 2/3/4
ras_subgroups.notes: Primary efficacy population in Douillard 2013. n=512 from abstract. Douillard 2015 Eur J Cancer reports n=505 RAS WT with tumor shrinkage data.

ras_subgroups.ras_status: KRAS exon 2 wild-type only (original analysis population)
ras_subgroups.mutation_detail: WT KRAS codons 12/13 only (includes patients with other RAS mutations)
ras_subgroups.notes: Original PRIME primary analysis (Douillard 2010 JCO, PMID 20921462): KRAS exon 2 WT PFS HR=0.80 (95%CI 0.66-0.97, P=0.02), OS HR=0.83 (95%CI 0.67-1.02, P=0.072). These are the KRAS exon 2-only HRs.

ras_subgroups.ras_status: RAS mutant (other RAS mutations beyond KRAS exon 2)
ras_subgroups.mutation_detail: KRAS exon 2 WT but mutant in KRAS exon 3 or 4, or NRAS exon 2, 3, or 4
ras_subgroups.notes: From Hecht 2014 AACR abstract (doi:10.1158/1557-3125.RASONC14-A57). These patients had KRAS exon 2 WT but harbored other RAS mutations — panitumumab showed no benefit (HR>1 for both PFS and OS, consistent with harm signal).
From original PRIME 2010 paper: KRAS exon 2 mutant PFS HR=1.29 (95%CI 1.04-1.62, P=0.02) — panitumumab harmful. OS HR=1.24 (95%CI 0.98-1.57, P=0.068).
Abstract states 'BRAF mutations were a negative prognostic factor' but does not report HR. Full-text table required. BRAF exon 15 was assessed in 639 KRAS exon 2 WT patients.

individual_ras_mutation_subgroups.note: Full-text Table 2 of Douillard 2013 NEJM reports individual mutation subgroups. Not accessible from abstract. From Oliner 2013 ASCO abstract (doi:10.1200/jco.2013.31.15_suppl.3511): individual RAS mutation subgroups by exon reported but truncated in literature search.
individual_ras_mutation_subgroups.full_text_accessibility: NEJM full text behind paywall; PMC equivalent not available

kras_exon2_only_hr_delta.pfs_hr_delta_interpretation: Expanded RAS WT population shows stronger panitumumab benefit (HR 0.72 vs 0.80) — delta of 0.08 improvement in HR by excluding other RAS mutations
kras_exon2_only_hr_delta.os_hr_delta_interpretation: Expanded RAS WT shows stronger OS benefit (HR 0.78 vs 0.83) — delta of 0.05 improvement in HR

expanded_ras_hr_delta.summary: Expanding from KRAS exon 2 only to full RAS panel (KRAS+NRAS exons 2/3/4) identified 17% additional mutation-positive patients (108/639 KRAS exon 2 WT). This enriched the WT population for panitumumab benefit: PFS HR improved from 0.80 to 0.72, OS HR improved from 0.83 to 0.78. The 108 patients with other RAS mutations showed harm signal (PFS HR=1.28, OS HR=1.29).
expanded_ras_hr_delta.proportion_reclassified: 17% of KRAS exon 2 WT patients reclassified as RAS mutant
expanded_ras_hr_delta.total_ras_mut_proportion: approximately 55% of all randomized patients (KRAS exon 2 mut ~37% + other RAS mut ~17% of remaining 63%)

data_completeness: GOOD for primary RAS-WT and other-RAS-mut subgroups. Individual mutation subgroup HRs (by specific exon/codon) require NEJM full-text access — not_accessible. BRAF subgroup HR not in abstract.
